disclaimer: Instrument qualification states the one question an instrument may answer, what it must never be cited for, and which refusal controls it has passed. It is not a security result: a qualified instrument can still miss a defect class its controls do not exercise, and no combination of instrument results proves constant-time behaviour, memory safety or compatibility. A PASS here means the instrument's own controls fired in the executing session; it is never evidence about the crate.

instruments.name: Valgrind memcheck with client requests (ctgrind)
instruments.intended_use: Detect secret-dependent control flow and secret-dependent memory addresses inside one function reached by a tainted input, at the source/IR level executed by memcheck.
not_its_use: constant-time behaviour under optimisation, or timing at all
microarchitectural leakage (caches, branch predictors, port contention)
a claim about the release DSO from a debug-profile test binary
coverage of paths the harness does not call

version_validation.identity_method: the harness is linked into a named binary and memcheck reports that binary's path; the crate's Rust ctgrind cases report the debug test binary SHA-256 in their receipts. The instrument does not itself identify the measured DSO, so each receipt records the DSO digest it linked and the test-binary digest.

failure_modes.false_positive: a tainted byte read for a non-secret reason (length normalisation, scratch reuse) is reported; the receipts classify each report rather than counting it as a leak
failure_modes.false_negative: a leaked path not executed by the harness, or a leak through an operation memcheck does not model is invisible; memcheck does not taint machine registers across an uninstrumented call
failure_modes.silent_truncation: memcheck continues after errors and its exit status is only 99 because --error-exitcode was set; without it a run with errors exits 0
failure_modes.unsupported_target: a binary compiled without debug information still runs, but the reported frames degrade to addresses
failure_modes.crash: valgrind itself can fail on an unsupported instruction or an unusual mapping; the run then has no classification and must not be counted
failure_modes.partial_output: a killed run leaves a prefix of the error list; the count is not a population
failure_modes.wrong_candidate: the harness links whatever library is on LD_LIBRARY_PATH; the receipt must record the DSO digest

soundness_limits: absence of reported errors means no secret-dependent branch or address use was observed on the executed path, at the sensitivity of memcheck's definedness model
it does not model value-only constant-latency effects, division latency, or microarchitecture
the crate-level ctgrind matrix runs a debug test binary: it establishes source-level dynamic observation, not release-binary timing assurance
the C harness is compiled -O1 -g for the control; it is not the shipped profile

scope.profile: debug test binary for the crate cases; -O1 -g C harness for the control
scope.statement: These runs establish source-level dynamic observation of secret-dependent branches and addresses. They do not establish release-binary timing behaviour, and they are not a constant-time result.

sensitivity_control.positive: cmpnaive: a deliberately early-exit comparator over a tainted buffer must report errors
sensitivity_control.negative: cmpcmp: the constant-time comparator over the same buffers must report no errors

cases.name: positive control (deliberately leaky comparator) fires
negative control (constant-time comparator) is clean

observed.detail: valgrind --tool=memcheck --error-exitcode=99; 99 is the configured error status, 0 is a clean run

fail_closed.refusal_text: a run whose harness did not execute (compile failure, missing DSO, valgrind failure) has no classification and is excluded from the matrix rather than reported as zero errors

instruments.name: dudect-style statistical timing harness

not_its_use: constant-time proof or a proof of absence of leakage
any statement about another CPU, another build profile or another optimisation level
a claim that a specific implementation ran: the harness records the flag it read back, not the dispatch
microarchitectural attribution

version_validation.identity_method: dudect has no version string. The pinned tree is commit dc269651fb2567e46755cfb2a13d3875592968b5 and the header digest above identifies the vendored copy actually compiled. The harness prints dudect.executed with the measurement count and dudect.flags with the BN flags it read back, and the receipt records the DSO digest.

components.header_location: court/tmp/tools/dudect/src/dudect.h (untracked scratch; not vendored in the repository)

failure_modes.false_positive: a class imbalance or a real measurement effect at the chosen sample size can cross the threshold; the harness crops, warms up and uses the upstream thresholds but the t statistic is still a sample statistic
failure_modes.false_negative: a small leak below the stated geometry is invisible; state 1 means only that no leakage evidence was found yet

failure_modes.wrong_candidate: the harness loads whatever LD_LIBRARY_PATH names; the receipt binds the measured DSO digest and the flag read-back

soundness_limits: absence of detected leakage is bounded evidence at the stated geometry, not proof of constant-time behaviour
no PMU and no frequency/SMT control at this venue: a null result is a null result on a virtualised host
the instrument measures wall-clock timing of one operation shape; it does not establish which implementation was dispatched
the harness's exit status is inverted relative to a gate: 0 means leakage found, 1 means no leakage evidence

scope.statement: Statistical timing of a release library on a virtualised host without a PMU. State 1 is no leakage evidence at this geometry, never constant time.

sensitivity_control.negative: cmpcmp: the constant-time comparator must produce state=1 (no leakage evidence)

failure_modes.false_positive: a document can be accepted while a premise it cites is false; acceptance is typing and algebra, not truth
failure_modes.false_negative: an obligation with no independently checkable procedure is still an obligation; the tool reports it rather than discharging it
failure_modes.silent_truncation: a claim set with a missing member is accepted as the smaller set; population completeness is the caller's obligation and is recorded in the document
failure_modes.unsupported_target: a claim naming an identity the tree check cannot resolve gets an obligation, not a pass
failure_modes.crash: a malformed document is refused with a JSON pointer
failure_modes.partial_output: an exclusion witness that is absent, unbound or self-authored is refused
failure_modes.wrong_candidate: a witness bound to a different candidate identity is refused

soundness_limits: no axis implies another: evidence, assumptions, TCB and obligations are orthogonal
denial by default is a typing rule, not a safety proof
reviewer identity and role are declared, not authenticated

scope.statement: A typing and algebra checker for claims. It never promotes a claim and never substitutes for instrument qualification.

sensitivity_control.negative: admitted exclusion witnesses without a valid binding, operation gating, malformed populations, duplicate keys and non-finite numbers are refused
